meta.name: NEET UG
meta.tagline: The single gateway to MBBS, BDS, AYUSH and veterinary seats across India.
meta.blurb: India's largest medical entrance. A full-length, NCERT-aligned mock across Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Zoology with instant scoring, negative marking and worked solutions.

pattern.marking: +4 for each correct answer, −1 for each wrong answer. Unattempted: 0.

briefing: NEET UG is the single national gate to every MBBS, BDS, AYUSH and veterinary seat in the country, and with well over twenty lakh candidates each year it is fiercely competitive — a handful of marks can move your rank by thousands. The paper rewards mastery of the NCERT textbooks above all: roughly half the paper is Biology (Botany + Zoology), so accuracy there is what separates top rankers. Physics is the usual deciding factor — it is formula-driven and time-sensitive, while Chemistry blends quick NCERT recall (especially Inorganic and Organic) with short calculations. With −1 negative marking, blind guessing is punished, so this mock reproduces the real pressure of choosing what to attempt. Every question here is original and built strictly to the NCERT-based NTA syllabus, and each carries a full explanation so the test doubles as revision.
strategy: Biology is 50% of the paper — bank it first; aim for near-perfect accuracy from NCERT lines.
Do Chemistry second: fast Inorganic/Organic recall, then short Physical-chemistry sums.
Leave Physics for a focused block; with −1 negatives, skip the 2–3 longest calculations if short on time.
Read assertion–reason and 'except/incorrect' stems twice — they are the commonest trap in NEET.

questions.q: The dimensional formula for pressure is the same as that of:
questions.explanation: Pressure $=\frac{F}{A}$ has dimensions $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$. Energy density $=\frac{E}{V}=\frac{ML^2T^{-2}}{L^3}=[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$, which matches pressure.

questions.q: If the percentage errors in measuring $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $1\%$, $2\%$ and $3\%$ respectively, the maximum percentage error in $X=\frac{A^2B}{C}$ is:
A body is projected vertically upward with speed $20\,\text{m/s}$. Taking $g=10\,\text{m/s}^2$, the maximum height reached is:
For a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ with speed $u$, the horizontal range is maximum when $\theta$ equals:
questions.explanation: $R=\frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$ is maximum when $\sin 2\theta=1$, i.e. $2\theta=90^\circ$, so $\theta=45^\circ$.

questions.q: A force of $20\,\text{N}$ acts on a body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ resting on a frictionless surface. The acceleration produced is:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ moving at $3\,\text{m/s}$ is brought to rest in $0.6\,\text{s}$. The average force applied is:
questions.explanation: $F=\frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}=\frac{m\Delta v}{\Delta t}=\frac{2\times3}{0.6}=10\,\text{N}$.

questions.q: A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is raised through a height of $4\,\text{m}$. The work done against gravity is (take $g=10\,\text{m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $W=mgh=5\times10\times4=200\,\text{J}$.

questions.q: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: $KE=\frac{1}{2}mv^2\propto v^2$. Doubling $v$ makes KE $2^2=4$ times the original.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is:
questions.explanation: All mass of a ring lies at distance $R$ from the axis, so $I=MR^2$.

questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass and radius roll down an incline. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.explanation: The solid sphere has smaller moment of inertia ($\frac{2}{5}MR^2 < \frac{2}{3}MR^2$), giving larger linear acceleration, so it reaches the bottom first.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the radius of the Earth $R$ above its surface is (where $g$ is surface value):
The escape velocity from the surface of a planet is independent of:
questions.explanation: $v_e=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$ depends on the planet's mass and radius and $G$, but not on the mass of the escaping body.

questions.q: Young's modulus has the same dimensions as:
questions.explanation: $Y=\frac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}}$; strain is dimensionless, so $Y$ has the dimensions of stress (pressure), $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$.

questions.q: According to Bernoulli's principle, when the speed of a flowing fluid increases, the pressure:
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation $P+\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2+\rho gh=\text{const}$ shows that where speed is higher, pressure is lower (at the same height).

questions.q: The rise of liquid in a capillary tube is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: $h=\frac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$, so the capillary rise is inversely proportional to the tube radius $r$.

questions.q: In an isothermal process for an ideal gas:
questions.explanation: Isothermal means constant temperature; for an ideal gas internal energy depends only on temperature, so $\Delta U=0$.

questions.q: A Carnot engine works between $400\,\text{K}$ and $300\,\text{K}$. Its efficiency is:
The root-mean-square speed of gas molecules is proportional to:
questions.explanation: $v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}\propto\sqrt{T}$, so rms speed varies as the square root of absolute temperature.

questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum of length $1\,\text{m}$ is (take $g=\pi^2\,\text{m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{1}{\pi^2}}=2\pi\cdot\frac{1}{\pi}=2\,\text{s}$.

questions.q: In SHM, the acceleration of the particle is:
options: directly proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position
questions.explanation: In SHM, $a=-\omega^2 x$; the magnitude is proportional to displacement and the acceleration is always directed towards the mean position.

questions.q: A wave has frequency $500\,\text{Hz}$ and wavelength $0.4\,\text{m}$. Its speed is:
questions.explanation: $v=f\lambda=500\times0.4=200\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.q: Two point charges of $+2\,\mu\text{C}$ and $+3\,\mu\text{C}$ are placed $30\,\text{cm}$ apart. The force between them (take $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}=9\times10^9$) is:
The electric field inside a charged hollow conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is:
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, the net charge enclosed inside the cavity is zero, so the electric field is zero everywhere inside a charged hollow conductor.

questions.q: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor increases when:
options: a dielectric is inserted between the plates
questions.explanation: $C=\frac{K\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$. Inserting a dielectric ($K>1$) increases capacitance; larger $d$ or smaller $A$ would decrease it.

questions.q: Three resistors of $2\,\Omega$, $3\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
The drift velocity of free electrons in a conductor is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: $v_d=\frac{eE\tau}{m}$, so drift velocity is directly proportional to the applied electric field $E$.

questions.q: A charged particle moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field experiences a force of magnitude:
questions.explanation: $F=qvB\sin\theta$. When velocity is parallel to $\vec{B}$, $\theta=0$, so $\sin\theta=0$ and the force is zero.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius $r$ carrying current $I$ with $N$ turns is:
questions.explanation: For a circular coil of $N$ turns, $B=\frac{\mu_0 N I}{2r}$ at its centre.

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic material is:
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have small negative susceptibility ($\chi<0$) and are weakly repelled by magnetic fields.

questions.q: A bar magnet of magnetic moment $M$ is cut into two equal halves perpendicular to its length. The magnetic moment of each half is:
questions.explanation: Cutting perpendicular to the length halves the length (and pole strength stays the same), so each piece has moment $\frac{M}{2}$.

questions.q: According to Lenz's law, the direction of the induced current is such that it:
options: has no relation to the flux change
opposes the change in flux that produces it
questions.explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux causing it, a consequence of conservation of energy.

questions.q: The rms value of an alternating current with peak value $I_0$ is:
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal AC, $I_{rms}=\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\approx0.707\,I_0$.

questions.q: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:
options: is in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor, the current lags the applied voltage by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ (i.e. $90^\circ$).

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves are:
questions.explanation: EM waves are transverse: the electric and magnetic fields oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.

questions.q: Which of the following has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In the EM spectrum, gamma rays have the highest frequency and therefore the shortest wavelength.

questions.q: An object is placed at the focus of a concave mirror. The image formed is:
questions.explanation: When the object is at the focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays become parallel, so the image is formed at infinity.

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, the fringe width is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: $\beta=\frac{\lambda D}{d}$, so the fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength $\lambda$.

questions.q: The power of a convex lens of focal length $25\,\text{cm}$ is:
questions.explanation: $P=\frac{1}{f(\text{in m})}=\frac{1}{0.25}=+4\,\text{D}$ (positive for a converging lens).

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of incident light (above threshold frequency) increases:
options: the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons
the number of photoelectrons emitted per second
questions.explanation: Intensity determines the number of photons per second, hence the photoelectron count. Maximum KE and stopping potential depend on frequency, not intensity.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is inversely proportional to its:
questions.explanation: $\lambda=\frac{h}{p}$, so the de Broglie wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum $p$.

questions.q: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, the radius of the $n$th orbit is proportional to:
questions.explanation: In Bohr's model, $r_n=\frac{n^2 h^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi m e^2}\propto n^2$.

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive sample is $10$ years. After $30$ years, the fraction of the original sample remaining is:
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives $=\frac{30}{10}=3$. Fraction remaining $=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3=\frac{1}{8}$.

questions.q: Assertion: Nuclear forces are charge-independent. Reason: Nuclear forces act equally between proton-proton, proton-neutron and neutron-neutron pairs. Choose the correct option.
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason correctly explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true, reason is false
Assertion is false, reason is true
questions.explanation: Nuclear forces are charge-independent, meaning they are nearly equal for p-p, p-n and n-n pairs. The reason directly explains the assertion.

questions.q: In an intrinsic semiconductor at absolute zero temperature, it behaves like:
questions.explanation: At $0\,\text{K}$ the valence band is full and the conduction band empty with no thermal excitation, so an intrinsic semiconductor behaves as a perfect insulator.

questions.q: Which dopant, when added to silicon, produces an n-type semiconductor?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is a pentavalent (group 15) element; it donates a free electron, producing an n-type semiconductor. Boron, aluminium and gallium are trivalent (p-type) dopants.

questions.q: The number of moles of oxygen atoms present in $5.6$ litre of $O_2$ gas at STP (molar volume $= 22.4\ \text{L mol}^{-1}$) is:
questions.explanation: Moles of $O_2 = 5.6/22.4 = 0.25$ mol. Each $O_2$ molecule has 2 O atoms, so moles of O atoms $= 0.25 \times 2 = 0.50$ mol.

questions.q: The number of radial nodes in a $3s$ orbital is:
questions.explanation: Radial nodes $= n - l - 1$. For $3s$: $n = 3$, $l = 0$, so radial nodes $= 3 - 0 - 1 = 2$.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is NOT permissible?
questions.explanation: For $n=2$, $l$ can be 0 or 1 only ($l = 0$ to $n-1$). $l=2$ is not allowed for $n=2$, so this set is invalid.

questions.q: The energy of an electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen is $-13.6\ \text{eV}$. The energy of the electron in the third orbit is:
For a reaction at constant temperature and pressure, $\Delta H = +30\ \text{kJ}$ and $\Delta S = +100\ \text{J K}^{-1}$. The temperature above which the reaction becomes spontaneous is:
questions.explanation: Spontaneous when $\Delta G < 0$, i.e. $\Delta H < T\Delta S$. $T > \Delta H/\Delta S = 30000/100 = 300$ K.

questions.q: Which of the following is an intensive property?
questions.explanation: Temperature is intensive (independent of amount of substance). Volume, enthalpy, and internal energy are extensive properties.

questions.q: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal reversible expansion, which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant temperature, $\Delta U = 0$ (U depends only on T). By the first law $q = -w$; heat absorbed equals work done by the gas. $\Delta H = 0$ as well.

questions.q: For the reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$, the relation between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is:
questions.explanation: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$ where $\Delta n = 2 - 4 = -2$. So $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2}$.

questions.q: The pH of a $0.001\ \text{M}$ HCl solution is:
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid, fully dissociated. $[H^+] = 10^{-3}$ M. $\text{pH} = -\log(10^{-3}) = 3$.

questions.q: The solubility product of AgCl is $1.6 \times 10^{-10}$. Its molar solubility in water is:
questions.explanation: For AgCl, $K_{sp} = s^2$. So $s = \sqrt{1.6 \times 10^{-10}} = 1.26 \times 10^{-5}$ M.

questions.q: The oxidation number of chromium in the dichromate ion $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is:
questions.explanation: Let oxidation number of Cr be $x$. $2x + 7(-2) = -2$, so $2x = 12$, $x = +6$.

questions.q: Which aqueous solution will have the lowest freezing point, assuming complete dissociation?
questions.explanation: Depression in freezing point depends on the number of particles (van't Hoff factor i). $CaCl_2$ gives $i=3$ (highest particle count among these), so it shows the greatest depression and lowest freezing point.

questions.q: Given $E^\circ_{Zn^{2+}/Zn} = -0.76\ \text{V}$ and $E^\circ_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = +0.34\ \text{V}$, the standard EMF of the Daniell cell is:
questions.explanation: $E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode} = 0.34 - (-0.76) = +1.10$ V.

questions.q: How much charge (in faradays) is required to deposit $0.5\ \text{mol}$ of aluminium from molten $Al_2O_3$?
questions.explanation: $Al^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Al$ requires 3 F per mole. For 0.5 mol: $0.5 \times 3 = 1.5$ F.

questions.q: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is $20\ \text{minutes}$. The time required for the concentration to reduce to one-fourth of its initial value is:
questions.explanation: Reducing to one-fourth requires two half-lives ($1 \rightarrow 1/2 \rightarrow 1/4$). Time $= 2 \times 20 = 40$ min.

questions.q: Which of the following has the largest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: K is in period 4, while Na, Mg, Al are in period 3. Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period, so K has the largest atomic radius.

questions.q: The correct order of first ionization enthalpy is:
questions.explanation: Expected order is Be > B (Be has stable filled $2s^2$). Across period 2: $B < Be < C < N$. B has lower IE than Be due to easy removal of the $2p$ electron.

questions.q: Which of the following exhibits the most negative (most exothermic) electron gain enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Chlorine has the most negative electron gain enthalpy. F is anomalously low due to its small size and high electron-electron repulsion in the compact 2p subshell.

questions.q: The hybridization of the central atom and shape of $SF_4$ are respectively:
questions.explanation: $SF_4$ has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on S, giving $sp^3d$ hybridization and a see-saw shape.

questions.q: According to molecular orbital theory, the bond order of the $O_2$ molecule is:
questions.explanation: $O_2$ has 16 electrons. Bond order $= (N_b - N_a)/2 = (10 - 6)/2 = 2$. $O_2$ is also paramagnetic due to two unpaired electrons in $\pi^*$ orbitals.

questions.q: Which of the following molecules has a non-zero dipole moment?
questions.explanation: $NH_3$ is pyramidal with a lone pair, giving a net dipole moment. $CO_2$ (linear), $BF_3$ (trigonal planar), and $CCl_4$ (tetrahedral) are symmetrical and have zero dipole moment.

questions.q: The number of sigma and pi bonds in a molecule of ethyne ($C_2H_2$) are respectively:
questions.explanation: $H-C\equiv C-H$ has 2 C-H sigma bonds, 1 C-C sigma bond (total 3 sigma) and 2 pi bonds in the triple bond.

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest reducing agent among the hydrides of group 15?
questions.explanation: Reducing character of group 15 hydrides increases down the group as the E-H bond weakens. $BiH_3$ is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.q: Which oxoacid of phosphorus is dibasic and a good reducing agent?
questions.explanation: $H_3PO_3$ has two P-OH bonds (dibasic) and one P-H bond, which makes it a reducing agent. $H_3PO_4$ is tribasic and not a reducing agent.

questions.q: The acidic strength order $HClO < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4$ of chlorine oxoacids is mainly due to:
options: Increasing number of oxygen atoms stabilising the conjugate base
questions.explanation: As the number of terminal oxygen atoms increases, the negative charge on the conjugate base is delocalised over more oxygen atoms, stabilising it and increasing acid strength.

questions.q: Which of the following $3d$ transition metal ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: $Sc^{3+}$ has a $3d^0$ configuration; with no d electrons, no d-d transitions are possible, so it is colourless. The others have partially filled d orbitals and are coloured.

questions.q: The lanthanoid contraction is responsible for the fact that:
options: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii
questions.explanation: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the expected increase in radius from Zr to Hf is offset, so Zr and Hf have nearly the same atomic and ionic radii and very similar chemistry.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of $[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3$ is:
questions.explanation: Six $NH_3$ ligands (hexaammine), Co with oxidation state +3 balancing three $Cl^-$. The cationic complex uses the metal name: hexaamminecobalt(III) chloride.

questions.q: The number of unpaired electrons in the complex ion $[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}$ (CN is a strong field ligand) is:
questions.explanation: Fe is +2 ($d^6$). With the strong field ligand $CN^-$, electrons pair up in the lower $t_{2g}$ set ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$), giving zero unpaired electrons (diamagnetic, low spin).

questions.q: According to crystal field theory, which ligand causes the largest splitting of d-orbitals (strongest field ligand)?
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series, $CN^-$ is among the strongest field ligands, causing the largest crystal field splitting. The order is $F^- < H_2O < NH_3 < CN^-$.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most stable carbocation?
questions.explanation: Carbocation stability increases with the number of alkyl groups due to +I effect and hyperconjugation: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl.

questions.q: Markovnikov's rule is followed in the addition of HBr to propene in the absence of peroxide. The major product is:
questions.explanation: Per Markovnikov's rule, H adds to the carbon with more H atoms, and Br to the more substituted carbon, forming the more stable secondary carbocation. The major product is 2-bromopropane.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is aromatic according to Huckel's rule?
questions.explanation: Benzene has 6 delocalised pi electrons ($4n+2$ with $n=1$), is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated, satisfying Huckel's rule. Cyclobutadiene ($4\pi$) is antiaromatic; cyclohexane is non-aromatic.

questions.q: The reagent used to convert benzene to acetophenone is:
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with acetyl chloride ($CH_3COCl$) in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ gives acetophenone ($C_6H_5COCH_3$).

questions.q: Which alkyl halide undergoes $S_N1$ reaction most readily?
questions.explanation: $S_N1$ rate depends on carbocation stability. Tert-butyl chloride forms the most stable tertiary carbocation, so it reacts fastest by the $S_N1$ mechanism.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene is less reactive than chloroethane towards nucleophilic substitution mainly because:
options: Chlorine is more electronegative in chlorobenzene
The C-Cl bond in chlorobenzene has partial double-bond character due to resonance
questions.explanation: In chlorobenzene, the lone pair on Cl delocalises into the ring, giving the C-Cl bond partial double-bond character. This shorter, stronger bond resists nucleophilic substitution.

questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
options: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
Phenol has a higher molar mass
Phenol contains a benzene ring only
questions.explanation: The phenoxide ion delocalises its negative charge over the aromatic ring through resonance, making it more stable than the ethoxide ion. Hence phenol is more acidic than ethanol.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds will NOT give a positive Tollens' test?
questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent oxidises aldehydes (giving a silver mirror) but not ketones. Acetone is a ketone, so it gives a negative Tollens' test.

questions.q: Which carbonyl compound undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction?
questions.explanation: The Cannizzaro reaction is given by aldehydes lacking an alpha-hydrogen. Benzaldehyde has no alpha-H and undergoes self oxidation-reduction with concentrated NaOH.

questions.q: In aqueous solution, the correct order of basic strength of methylamine, dimethylamine and ammonia is:
questions.explanation: In aqueous medium the order (balancing +I effect, solvation and steric factors) is $(CH_3)_2NH > CH_3NH_2 > NH_3$. Dimethylamine is the strongest base of these three in water.

questions.q: The carbylamine reaction (formation of foul-smelling isocyanide with $CHCl_3$ and alcoholic KOH) is a test for:
questions.explanation: Only primary amines react with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to give foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamines). It is a confirmatory test for primary amines.

questions.q: Aniline on diazotisation at $0-5^\circ C$ with $NaNO_2/HCl$ gives:
questions.explanation: Aniline reacts with nitrous acid (from $NaNO_2/HCl$) at low temperature ($0-5^\circ C$) to form benzene diazonium chloride ($C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-$).

questions.q: Which of the following is a reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: Glucose has a free aldehyde (hemiacetal) group and reduces Tollens'/Fehling's reagent. Sucrose is non-reducing (anomeric carbons linked); starch and cellulose are polysaccharides.

questions.q: The bond that links two amino acids in a protein is:
questions.explanation: Amino acids are joined by peptide (amide) bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, with loss of water.

questions.q: Which vitamin is water-soluble and its deficiency causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is water-soluble; its deficiency causes scurvy. Vitamins A, D, and K are fat-soluble.

questions.q: In the binomial name Mangifera indica, the word 'indica' represents the:
questions.explanation: In a binomial name the first word denotes the genus (Mangifera) and the second word denotes the specific epithet (indica). NCERT calls the second component the specific epithet.

questions.q: Which taxonomic category is described as a group of related families possessing a few similar characters?
questions.explanation: As per NCERT, Order is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters. The order Polymoniales includes families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae.

questions.q: Population growth under limited resources, regulated by the carrying capacity (K), is represented by a:
questions.explanation: Logistic growth with limited resources gives a sigmoid (S-shaped) Verhulst-Pearl logistic curve. Exponential growth with unlimited resources gives a J-shaped curve.

questions.q: In R.H. Whittaker's five kingdom classification, the main criteria used included all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Presence of a cell wall as the sole criterion
questions.explanation: Whittaker (1969) used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. Cell wall presence alone was not a criterion; it varies within kingdoms.

questions.q: Which group is regarded as a connecting link between plants and animals, being photosynthetic in light but heterotrophic in darkness?
questions.explanation: Euglenoids (e.g., Euglena) lack a cell wall (having a protein-rich pellicle), are photosynthetic in sunlight but heterotrophic in darkness — hence a bridge between plants and animals.

questions.q: The smallest living cells known, which completely lack a cell wall and many of which are pathogenic, are the:
questions.explanation: NCERT states Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen and many are pathogenic.

questions.q: In which plant group is the dominant, free-living, photosynthetic phase the haploid gametophyte?
questions.explanation: In bryophytes the main plant body is the haploid gametophyte; the sporophyte is dependent on it. In pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms the diploid sporophyte is dominant.

questions.q: Gymnosperms are said to bear 'naked seeds' because:
options: Ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and seeds remain exposed
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms ovules are not enclosed within an ovary wall and remain exposed before and after fertilisation; the resulting seeds are 'naked', i.e., not covered by a fruit.

questions.q: The red colour of members of Rhodophyceae is mainly due to the predominance of the pigment:
questions.explanation: NCERT attributes the red colour of red algae (Rhodophyceae) to the predominance of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin. Fucoxanthin is characteristic of brown algae.

questions.q: Aestivation in which the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction is termed:
questions.explanation: In imbricate aestivation the margins overlap but not in any particular direction, as in Cassia and Gulmohur. Twisted aestivation has a regular overlapping direction.

questions.q: The androecium of family Fabaceae is correctly described as:
options: Diadelphous, with nine stamens fused and one free
questions.explanation: Fabaceae (papilionaceous) has a diadelphous androecium, stamens (9)+1 — nine stamens fused into one bundle and the tenth stamen remaining free.

questions.q: The edible part of a coconut is the:
questions.explanation: Coconut is a fibrous drupe; its edible white kernel and coconut water are the endosperm. The fibrous husk is the mesocarp and the hard shell is the endocarp.

questions.q: Casparian strips, band-like deposits of suberin, are characteristically present in the:
questions.explanation: Endodermal cells of the root bear Casparian strips — band-like thickenings of suberin on their radial and tangential walls — which regulate water entry into the vascular tissue.

questions.q: Which feature correctly distinguishes a dicot stem from a monocot stem?
options: Vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and open
Vascular bundles are closed and lack cambium
questions.explanation: In dicot stems vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and open (cambium present, allowing secondary growth), arranged in a ring. Monocot stems have scattered, closed bundles lacking cambium.

questions.q: The activity of the cork cambium (phellogen) produces phellem and phelloderm, which together with phellogen constitute the:
questions.explanation: Phellogen cuts off phellem (cork) outwards and phelloderm (secondary cortex) inwards. Phellogen, phellem and phelloderm together constitute the periderm.

questions.q: The single-membrane-bound organelle rich in hydrolytic enzymes that are optimally active at acidic pH is the:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles formed by the Golgi apparatus, rich in hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at acidic pH.

questions.q: According to the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane (Singer and Nicolson, 1972), which statement is correct?
options: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid allows lateral movement of proteins
The lipid bilayer is completely rigid
Membrane is made only of proteins
Proteins occur only on the outer surface
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model holds that the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer enables lateral movement of proteins; membrane fluidity supports functions like endocytosis and cell growth.

questions.q: The 70S ribosomes found in prokaryotes, chloroplasts and mitochondria are composed of subunits of:
questions.explanation: A 70S ribosome consists of a larger 50S and a smaller 30S subunit. The eukaryotic 80S ribosome is made of 60S and 40S subunits.

questions.q: DNA replication (synthesis) during the cell cycle takes place in the:
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs in the S (synthesis) phase of interphase; DNA content per cell doubles, while chromosome number stays the same.

questions.q: Synapsis (pairing of homologous chromosomes) occurs during which sub-stage of prophase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: During zygotene the homologous chromosomes start pairing (synapsis) forming the synaptonemal complex. Crossing over occurs later, during pachytene.

questions.q: Centromeres split and sister chromatids separate to move towards opposite poles during:
questions.explanation: In mitotic anaphase the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles. In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) separate.

questions.q: The primary CO2 acceptor in the C4 (Hatch and Slack) pathway is:
questions.explanation: In C4 plants the primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells is the 3-carbon molecule phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), with PEP carboxylase as the enzyme. RuBP is the acceptor in the Calvin cycle.

questions.q: Photolysis (splitting) of water during photosynthesis is associated with:
options: Photosystem I on the stromal side
The stroma during the Calvin cycle
Photosystem II on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane
Photosystem I on the outer surface
questions.explanation: Photolysis of water is linked to Photosystem II and occurs on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane, releasing O2, protons and electrons.

questions.q: The special leaf anatomy of C4 plants, in which bundle-sheath cells form wreath-like rings around the vascular bundles, is called:
questions.explanation: C4 plants show Kranz anatomy: large bundle-sheath cells form rings around vascular bundles, with many chloroplasts, thick walls and no intercellular spaces.

questions.q: The net gain of ATP from the complete aerobic oxidation of one molecule of glucose, as given in NCERT, is:
questions.explanation: NCERT states a net gain of 38 ATP molecules from the complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose molecule under the assumptions specified in the text.

questions.q: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) takes place in the:
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, whereas glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and the electron transport chain lies on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four major causes of biodiversity loss described in NCERT as the 'Evil Quartet'?
questions.explanation: The 'Evil Quartet' — the four major causes of biodiversity loss — are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions, and co-extinctions. Genetic recombination is not among them.

questions.q: Which plant hormone promotes senescence and abscission, induces seed dormancy, and is called the 'stress hormone' because it closes stomata under water stress?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) promotes senescence and abscission, induces seed dormancy and is called the stress hormone because it closes stomata and increases stress tolerance.

questions.q: Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases yield mainly by:
options: Increasing the length of the stem (internode elongation)
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that gibberellins increase the length of the sugarcane stem, raising the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

questions.q: Which statement about the gaseous plant growth regulator ethylene is correct?
options: It hastens fruit ripening and promotes senescence and abscission
It delays senescence of plant organs
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous PGR that hastens fruit ripening, promotes senescence and abscission, breaks seed and bud dormancy, and induces flowering in pineapple.

questions.q: The innermost wall layer of the anther, which nourishes the developing pollen grains, is the:
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost anther wall layer; it nourishes developing pollen grains and its cells have dense cytoplasm, often with more than one nucleus.

questions.q: Double fertilisation in angiosperms results in the formation of the:
options: Zygote and the primary endosperm nucleus
questions.explanation: In double fertilisation one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) forming the diploid zygote, while the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.q: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is:
questions.explanation: A mature embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate: three antipodals, two synergids, one egg cell and one central cell with two polar nuclei (8 nuclei but 7 cells).

questions.q: The F2 phenotypic ratio obtained in a Mendelian dihybrid cross is:
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross gives an F2 phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1, the basis of Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.

questions.q: Incomplete dominance, where the F1 phenotype is intermediate between the two parents, is classically illustrated by flower colour in:
questions.explanation: In Antirrhinum (snapdragon), a cross of red (RR) and white (rr) gives pink (Rr) in F1 — incomplete dominance, with an intermediate F1 phenotype.

questions.q: A cross used to determine the genotype of an organism showing the dominant phenotype, by crossing it with the homozygous recessive parent, is called a:
questions.explanation: A test cross crosses an individual of unknown genotype showing the dominant phenotype with the homozygous recessive parent, revealing whether it is homozygous or heterozygous.

questions.q: Conclusive proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the bacteriophage experiments of:
questions.explanation: Hershey and Chase (1952) used radiolabelled bacteriophages (32P for DNA, 35S for protein) to show that DNA, not protein, enters the host bacterium and is the genetic material.

questions.q: In the Watson–Crick model of DNA, the number of hydrogen bonds between guanine and cytosine is:
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, while guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds, as described by the Watson–Crick double helix model.

questions.q: In the lac operon of E. coli, the repressor protein that binds to the operator is coded by the:
questions.explanation: The i gene (regulatory gene) codes for the repressor protein, which binds the operator and switches off transcription of the structural genes z, y and a in the absence of lactose.

questions.q: The large holes in Swiss cheese are produced by a large amount of CO2 generated by the bacterium:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the large holes in Swiss cheese are due to a large amount of CO2 produced by a bacterium named Propionibacterium sharmanii.

questions.q: Rhizobium, an important biofertiliser, fixes atmospheric nitrogen while living in:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacterium that resides in the root nodules of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by the plant.

questions.q: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressive drug in organ-transplant patients, is produced by the fungus:
questions.explanation: Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressant for organ-transplant patients, is produced by Trichoderma polysporum. Statins, which lower blood cholesterol, come from Monascus purpureus.

questions.q: An interaction in which one species benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefited is called:
questions.explanation: In commensalism one species benefits and the other is unaffected, e.g., an orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch, or barnacles living on a whale.

questions.q: A big tree supporting numerous insects and then fewer birds best exemplifies a(n):
questions.explanation: A single tree (producer) supporting a large number of insects (primary consumers) gives an inverted pyramid of numbers. The pyramid of energy is always upright.

questions.q: Conservation of biodiversity by protecting whole ecosystems, as in biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries, is termed:
questions.explanation: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats by conserving whole ecosystems (biosphere reserves, national parks, sanctuaries, sacred groves). Ex situ uses botanical gardens, zoos and seed banks.

questions.q: Which of the following animal groups is characterised by the presence of cnidoblasts or cnidocytes?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that Coelenterata (Cnidaria) are characterised by the presence of cnidoblasts/cnidocytes on the tentacles and body, used for anchorage, defence and capturing prey. Comb plates are the diagnostic feature of Ctenophora.

questions.q: Bioluminescence (the property of a living organism to emit light) is well marked in which phylum?
questions.explanation: NCERT specifically notes that bioluminescence is well marked in Ctenophora (sea walnuts / comb jellies). They are exclusively marine and use comb plates for locomotion.

questions.q: Gene therapy was first used in 1990 to treat a four-year-old girl suffering from a disorder caused by the deficiency of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: NCERT states the first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a girl with ADA (adenosine deaminase) deficiency, an enzyme crucial for the immune system; the deficiency causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID).

questions.q: The epithelium in which cells appear to be in multiple layers, but in reality all cells touch the basement membrane, is called:
questions.explanation: NCERT describes pseudostratified epithelium where the nuclei lie at different levels giving a false (pseudo) impression of layering, yet every cell contacts the basement membrane. It lines the trachea and large bronchi.

questions.q: Which type of muscle tissue is striated, involuntary and uninucleate (mostly), with cells joined by intercalated discs?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle of the heart is striated and involuntary; its cells are joined end to end by intercalated discs. Skeletal muscle is striated but voluntary; smooth (visceral) muscle is unstriated and involuntary.

questions.q: In the cockroach, the blood vascular system is open type and the blood is colourless. The blood is called:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the cockroach has an open circulatory system; the colourless blood (lacking respiratory pigment) is termed haemolymph and bathes the visceral organs directly in sinuses.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most abundant protein in the animal world and the whole of the biosphere, respectively, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation: NCERT states collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world, whereas RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate Carboxylase-Oxygenase) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.

questions.q: An enzyme lowers the rate of a reaction by lowering which of the following?
questions.explanation: NCERT explains that enzymes increase reaction rate by lowering the activation energy barrier (the energy difference between substrate and the transition state), without altering the equilibrium of the reaction.

questions.q: The bond formed between two amino acids during protein synthesis is a:
questions.explanation: NCERT states amino acids are linked by peptide bonds, formed between the carboxyl (–COOH) group of one amino acid and the amino (–NH2) group of the next. Glycosidic bonds link monosaccharides; phosphodiester bonds link nucleotides.

questions.q: Which enzyme in saliva begins the digestion of starch in the buccal cavity, and what is the approximate fraction of starch hydrolysed there?
questions.explanation: NCERT states salivary amylase (ptyalin) hydrolyses about 30% of starch into maltose in the buccal cavity at pH 6.8. Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach; trypsin in the small intestine.

questions.q: The proenzyme pepsinogen is converted into active pepsin by:
questions.explanation: NCERT states HCl secreted by parietal (oxyntic) cells converts inactive pepsinogen into active pepsin and provides the acidic pH (1.8) optimal for pepsin. Enterokinase activates trypsinogen, not pepsinogen.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of layers in the wall of the alimentary canal from outside to inside?
questions.explanation: NCERT describes four layers from outside (lumen-distal) to inside (lumen-proximal): serosa, muscularis, sub-mucosa and mucosa. The mucosa is the innermost layer lining the lumen.

questions.q: The volume of air that can be breathed in by a forced inspiration, which is the maximum amount that can be inspired, is termed:
questions.explanation: Inspiratory Capacity (IC) = Tidal Volume + Inspiratory Reserve Volume, i.e., the total volume a person can inspire after a normal expiration. Vital Capacity includes expiratory reserve as well.

questions.q: What percentage of carbon dioxide is transported in the blood in the form of bicarbonate (HCO3-)?
questions.explanation: NCERT states about 70% of CO2 is transported as bicarbonate, around 20-25% bound to haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin, and about 7% dissolved in plasma.

questions.q: The enzyme carbonic anhydrase, important in CO2 transport, is present in high concentration in:
questions.explanation: NCERT states carbonic anhydrase is present in very high concentration in RBCs and in minute amounts in plasma; it catalyses the reversible reaction between CO2 and water to form carbonic acid (and then bicarbonate).

questions.q: The pacemaker of the human heart, which generates the wave of contraction, is the:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the Sino-atrial node (SAN), located in the right upper corner of the right atrium, has the highest rate of action potential generation (70-75 per minute) and is therefore called the pacemaker.

questions.q: Universal recipients are individuals with blood group AB. This is because their blood:
options: Has both antibodies anti-A and anti-B in plasma
Has neither antigen A nor antigen B on RBCs
Has both antigens A and B but no antibodies in plasma
Has antigen A and antibody anti-B
questions.explanation: NCERT states group AB individuals have both antigens A and B on their RBCs but no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma, so they can accept blood from all groups, making them universal recipients.

questions.q: Which of the following blood cells is involved in the coagulation (clotting) of blood?
questions.explanation: NCERT states thrombocytes (platelets) are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes; they release factors involved in the coagulation or clotting of blood. A reduced platelet count can lead to clotting disorders.

questions.q: Humans are ureotelic, meaning the chief nitrogenous excretory product is:
questions.explanation: NCERT classifies humans as ureotelic; ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into less toxic urea in the liver via the ornithine cycle and excreted by the kidneys. Ammonotelic animals excrete ammonia; uricotelic animals excrete uric acid.

questions.q: The process by which the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) actively secretes H+, K+ and ammonia into the filtrate helps maintain:
options: The ionic and acid-base balance of body fluids
questions.explanation: NCERT states the PCT helps to maintain the ionic balance and acid-base balance of body fluids by selective secretion of H+, NH3 (ammonia) and K+ ions into the filtrate and by reabsorption of HCO3- from it.

questions.q: The hormone that increases the reabsorption of water (facultative) from the distal parts of the tubule, thereby reducing diuresis, is:
questions.explanation: NCERT states ADH (vasopressin) facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule, preventing diuresis. A fall in body fluid volume activates osmoreceptors that stimulate ADH release from the neurohypophysis.

questions.q: According to the sliding filament theory, muscle contraction occurs because:
options: Thin (actin) filaments slide over thick (myosin) filaments
questions.explanation: NCERT's sliding filament theory states that contraction occurs as the thin (actin) filaments slide over the thick (myosin) filaments; the length of the A-band remains constant while the I-band and H-zone shorten.

questions.q: Which protein covers the active (binding) sites on actin in a resting muscle, preventing cross-bridge formation?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that in the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments; tropomyosin runs along the actin and, with troponin, covers these sites until Ca2+ binds troponin.

questions.q: The number of bones in the human skull (cranial bones) and the total number of bones in the axial skeleton are, respectively:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the human skull is composed of 8 cranial bones (plus 14 facial bones) and the axial skeleton comprises 80 bones (skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs).

questions.q: During the depolarisation phase of a nerve impulse, the membrane becomes more permeable to which ion, causing the inside to become positive?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that on stimulation, the membrane becomes freely permeable to Na+; the rapid influx of Na+ reverses the polarity (inside becomes positive, outside negative), producing depolarisation and the action potential.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain is called the 'thermostat' of the body and controls hunger, thirst and body temperature?
questions.explanation: NCERT states the hypothalamus contains centres that control body temperature, urge for eating and drinking; it also secretes hormones (releasing/inhibiting). The medulla controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes.

questions.q: In the human eye, the photoreceptor cells that function in dim light (twilight vision) and contain the pigment rhodopsin are the:
questions.explanation: NCERT states rods contain the purplish-red pigment rhodopsin (visual purple), which contains a derivative of vitamin A, and are responsible for twilight (scotopic) vision. Cones are responsible for daylight and colour vision.

questions.q: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the alpha-cells of the islets of Langerhans?
questions.explanation: NCERT states the islets of Langerhans contain alpha-cells secreting glucagon (a hyperglycaemic hormone) and beta-cells secreting insulin (a hypoglycaemic hormone). Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

questions.q: The hormone thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland, requires which element for its synthesis?
questions.explanation: NCERT states iodine is essential for the normal rate of synthesis of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4); its dietary deficiency leads to goitre, an enlargement of the thyroid gland.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline, called emergency hormones. Reason (R): These catecholamines are rapidly secreted in response to stress and during emergencies. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT states the adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), collectively called catecholamines. They are rapidly secreted in response to stress and are termed emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight, so R correctly explains A.

questions.q: The process of release of an ovum from a mature Graafian follicle is called ovulation. It is induced by a surge of which hormone?
questions.explanation: NCERT states the rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum (ovulation) is induced by a rapid surge of LH (the LH surge) during the middle of the cycle (around the 14th day).

questions.q: After ovulation, the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into a structure that secretes large amounts of progesterone. This structure is the:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone essential for maintenance of the endometrium needed for implantation.

questions.q: The fluid-filled cavity of the blastocyst is called the blastocoel, and the inner group of cells that gives rise to the embryo is the:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the blastocyst has an outer trophoblast layer (which attaches to the endometrium) and an inner group of cells called the inner cell mass, which differentiates into the embryo proper.

questions.q: Which contraceptive method works by preventing/retarding the entry of sperms, ovulation and implantation, and also alters the quality of cervical mucus?
questions.explanation: NCERT states oral pills containing progestogens (or progestogen-oestrogen combinations) inhibit ovulation and implantation, and alter the quality of cervical mucus to retard/prevent entry of sperms. Saheli is a once-a-week non-steroidal pill.

questions.q: The full form of the technique 'ZIFT', an assisted reproductive technology, is:
questions.explanation: NCERT defines ZIFT as Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer, in which the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube. Transfer of an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus is called IUT.

questions.q: Amniocentesis, a foetal sex-determination test based on chromosomal patterns in the amniotic fluid, is legally banned in India because it is misused for:
questions.explanation: NCERT states that although amniocentesis can detect genetic disorders, it is statutorily banned for sex determination because it is being misused to abort the normal female foetus (female foeticide).

questions.q: Malignant malaria, the most serious form, is caused by which species of Plasmodium?
questions.explanation: NCERT states Plasmodium falciparum causes the most serious, malignant malaria, which can prove fatal. The malarial parasite is transmitted by the bite of the infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.q: In recombinant DNA technology, the commonly used vector pBR322 is an example of a:
questions.explanation: NCERT describes pBR322 as a well-known plasmid cloning vector with an origin of replication (ori), selectable markers (ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes) and recognition sites for restriction enzymes.

questions.q: AIDS is caused by HIV, which primarily attacks and destroys which cells of the immune system?
questions.explanation: NCERT states HIV (a retrovirus) enters macrophages and helper T-lymphocytes (TH), where it replicates; the progressive decrease in the number of helper T-cells weakens immunity, leading to AIDS.

questions.q: The forelimbs of a whale, a bat, a cheetah and a human have a similar anatomical structure but perform different functions. Such organs are called:
questions.explanation: NCERT states that homologous organs have similar structure and origin but different functions (e.g., forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah, human); they indicate divergent evolution. Analogous organs have different structure but similar function (convergent evolution).

questions.q: Bt cotton is resistant to certain insect pests because it has been engineered to produce a toxin gene from the bacterium:
questions.explanation: NCERT states the Bt toxin gene (cry genes) has been cloned from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis and expressed in plants such as Bt cotton to provide resistance against insects. The protein crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein.

questions.q: The classic example of natural selection studied during industrialisation in England, involving the moth Biston betularia, is known as:
questions.explanation: NCERT describes industrial melanism: before industrialisation white-winged moths predominated; after industrialisation, dark-winged (melanic) moths were better camouflaged on soot-covered trees and were selected, illustrating natural selection.

questions.q: Restriction endonucleases are sometimes called 'molecular scissors' because they:
options: Cut DNA at specific recognition sequences
questions.explanation: NCERT states restriction endonucleases recognise a specific palindromic sequence in DNA and cut both strands a little away from the centre, producing sticky ends; this site-specific cutting earns them the name molecular scissors. DNA ligase joins fragments.

questions.q: In Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the enzyme used for the extension of primers because it can tolerate the high denaturation temperature is:
questions.explanation: NCERT states PCR uses a thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase, isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus) which remains active during the high temperature of denaturation, enabling repeated cycles of amplification.

questions.q: The first transgenic cow, named 'Rosie', produced human protein-enriched milk. The milk contained which human protein?
questions.explanation: NCERT states the transgenic cow Rosie produced human protein-enriched milk (2.4 grams per litre) containing the human alpha-lactalbumin, which is nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow milk.
